previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for post-procedural observation following his fifth transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for a 2.7 cm tumor in hepatic segment VIII. The procedure was successfully performed via the right hepatic artery using doxorubicin-loaded Oncozene beads, with minor additional supply noted from the left hepatic artery that was not amenable to treatment. He tolerated the intervention well without immediate complications, remained hemodynamically stable, and reported no pain, nausea, or procedural site issues. His cirrhosis, diabetes, and other comorbidities were managed with continuation of home medications. A mild increase in right leg edema was noted, attributed to dietary salt intake. He was discharged home the following day in stable condition with instructions to monitor for fever or pain, continue all prescribed medications, and follow up with his liver team in two weeks for evaluation and planning.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
